run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T04:47:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Alertmanager reports RequestErrorRate for otel-demo/frontend-proxy (payload annotation value 0.0111). The exposed span metrics confirm that frontend-proxy emits error spans on exactly two operations: 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT). Two distinct error patterns are visible in the authorized window. (1) Sporadic proxy-level failures before the alert start: the frontend-proxy access log records 14 responses '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for GET /api/products/*, /api/data, /api/recommendations and /api/cart between 04:28:19Z and 04:46:04Z, i.e. before the alert's 04:47:17Z start, plus identical 503 UC responses at 04:48:04Z and 04:51:04-04:51:05Z; these are responses where the frontend upstream closed the connection before responding. (2) A sharp burst: frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500 ('500 - via_upstream', 21-byte bodies) for POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout from 04:49:51.371Z to at least 04:50:19.935Z, and the frontend's own error spans in the matching metric windows are on grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, GET/POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and tcp.connect. That burst begins ~1.4 s after Deployment otel-demo/cart replaced its only pod in a rollout restart (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d, pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:49:47Z, old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 killed 04:49:50Z). The replacement cart pod was reported Ready at 04:49:50Z, but its log shows 'Successfully connected to Redis' only at 04:50:03.611Z and feature-provider initialization from 04:50:08.012Z, and the pod template defines no readiness probe, so the single-endpoint cart Service had no serving backend in that gap. cart's own error-span series is 0 and it handled calls normally from 04:51:43Z, so the cart application itself did not fail. The flagd-config setting cartFailure='on' ('Fail cart service') matches the failure path by name but is not confirmed as active cause. The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the registered Prometheus, and the exposed metric reads 0 at the 04:47:17Z sample, so the alert's exact evaluation cannot be reproduced; the onset is best explained by the sporadic upstream-connection-termination 503s (hypothesis), while the dominant burst has a traced mechanism (cart rollout without readiness gating). Conclusion is partial: the alert expression and the origin of the 503 UC behaviour remain unverified.

claims.text: traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=frontend-proxy carries error spans on exactly two series: span_name='ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and span_name='router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); the 5-minute error rate on 'ingress' reaches 0.35185/s and on 'router frontend egress' 0.34444/s at the sample timestamped 2026-11-17T04:51:17Z, while both series read 0 at the samples timestamped 04:44:17Z, 04:45:17Z, 04:46:17Z and 04:47:17Z.

At 15-second resolution the frontend-proxy error rate is 3.1/s in the two 1-minute windows ending 04:51:00Z and 04:51:15Z and 0 from 04:51:30Z onward; frontend's own error rates in those same windows are grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.55-0.74/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 1.05-1.48/s, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.6/s, GET /api/cart 0.55-0.74/s, POST /api/cart 1.05-1.48/s, POST /api/checkout 0.6/s, GET 0.77/s, POST 2.33/s and tcp.connect 0.23/s.

The frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt logged 14 responses of the form '"GET /api/products/... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' (also /api/data, /api/recommendations and /api/cart) between 04:28:19.488Z and 04:46:04.252Z, i.e. before the alert start of 04:47:17Z, and further identical 503 UC responses at 04:48:04.246Z and at 04:51:04.718Z/04:51:04.962Z/04:51:05.007Z.

Between 04:49:51.371Z and 04:50:19.935Z the frontend-proxy pod returned 93 HTTP 500 responses in the form '"POST /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' (also GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout) with 21-byte response bodies; the log view returned the newest 100 of 426 matching lines, so later 500s inside the queried window are unknown.

Deployment otel-demo/cart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/revision=2) scaled ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1 at 04:49:47Z and cart-755465879b from 1 to 0 at 04:49:50Z (event 'Deleted pod: cart-755465879b-rh5r4'); the new pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was scheduled at 04:49:47Z, had Ready condition True at 04:49:50Z and is owned by ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d.

The ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d pod template differs from cart-755465879b only by the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T04:49:47Z (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, same env), and neither template defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe for the cart container.

In the window 04:49:45Z-04:50:10Z the replacement cart container logged exactly three lines: 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 04:50:03.611Z, 'Initializing the Feature Lifecycle Manager for state {State}.' at 04:50:07.413Z and 'Starting initialization of the feature provider' at 04:50:08.012Z - i.e. application initialization was still running after the pod was reported Ready at 04:49:50Z and after the first cart 500 at 04:49:51.371Z.

The cart Service currently has exactly one endpoint (pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz, port 8080), while frontend has one endpoint (frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8) and frontend-proxy one (frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt).

The cart service recorded no error spans: its status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR series is 0 at every returned point from 04:52:17Z to 05:04:17Z, and the new cart pod logged normal AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync calls from 04:51:43Z onward.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) declares flag 'cartFailure' with defaultVariant 'on' and description 'Fail cart service', while every other fault flag it defines (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is 'off', as read at ~05:10Z.

The fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh was terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled at 04:55:17Z and restarted at 04:55:18Z (restartCount 1); the frontend-proxy 5-minute error rate had already dropped from 0.36296/s at 04:55:17Z to 0.01852/s at 04:56:17Z.

get_metric_names for {service_name="frontend-proxy"} returned only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so no HTTP status-code or gRPC status-code series are available for this service in this target's Prometheus.

The exposed frontend-proxy span metrics only have samples from about 04:29-04:34 onward in the queried windows (source_start_at 04:29:17Z in one query and 04:33:30Z in a 10-minute-rate query), so there is no baseline for the error rate before ~04:29Z.

The alert's start at 04:47:17Z most plausibly reflects a single sporadically failing request: the only frontend-proxy error evidence around that time is the '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' response logged at 04:46:04Z, and the reported value 0.0111 equals 1/90 (one error averaged over ~90 s). The exposed span-metric sample at 04:47:17Z reads 0, so this cannot be confirmed without the alert's expression and a complete metric timeline.

The /api/cart and /api/checkout failures of 04:49:51-04:50:20Z were caused by the cart Deployment's rollout leaving the single-replica cart Service without a serving backend: the old pod was killed at 04:49:50Z, the replacement became the sole Service endpoint on container start with no readiness probe, and the cart application only finished Redis/feature-provider initialization after 04:50:08Z; the client-side failures appear in the span metrics about a minute later than in the access log.

The '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses indicate the frontend upstream closed a reused connection before the response started (an Envoy upstream keep-alive/idle-timeout mismatch), not an application error in frontend: the affected requests returned 95-byte 503s with no upstream response time, and at those moments the frontend produced no error spans. The Envoy configuration and the frontend keep-alive settings that would confirm this are not observable in this target.

The flagd-config cartFailure='on' setting is a fault-injection candidate whose declared fault ('Fail cart service') matches the observed cart-call failure path, but the evidence does not confirm it acted as the cause during this incident; it remains unverified because the flagd service and cart flag-evaluation logs produced no readable lines.

cart serving calls normally from 04:51:43Z while cart's own error-span series stays 0 and flagd-config still shows cartFailure='on' (read at ~05:10Z) argues against an active cart-failure flag being the source of the 04:49:51-04:50:20Z 500 burst.

fraud-detection's OOMKill is not the cause of this frontend-proxy error signal: it occurred at 04:55:17Z, after the frontend-proxy error rate had already collapsed (0.01852/s at 04:56:17Z) and while frontend error spans were 0, and fraud-detection's own error-span rate never exceeds 0.0037/s in the window.

Add a readinessProbe (and livenessProbe) to the cart Deployment and the other otel-demo workloads so a pod only receives Service traffic after the application serves, and avoid replacing a single-replica service without readiness gating (surge/PDB or a second replica), which is the concrete gap that let cart disappear from the Service for ~30 s.

Align the frontend-proxy upstream connection-pool idle timeout with the frontend HTTP keep-alive (or disable upstream connection reuse) to eliminate the repeated 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' 503s that keep the error rate above zero between cart incidents.

Raise the RequestErrorRate threshold above 0 and/or add a sustained 'for' duration with an evaluation window long enough to survive collector batch lag, so a single transient 503 does not fire a warning.
Have the flagd-config owner confirm whether cartFailure is intentionally 'on'; if it was set for testing it should be reverted, since it is a live fault-injection switch on the cart service.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the registered Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no rules, so the expression, evaluation window and the meaning of the reported 0.0111 are unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so it is unknown who or what applied the cart Deployment rollout restart at 04:49:47Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) and whether flagd-config cartFailure changed during the window.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend or frontend-proxy in any queried window (04:40-05:08Z, 04:45-05:08Z, 04:48-05:08Z, 05:04-05:08Z), so no span-level error details, error messages or parent-child call edges are available.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 04:49-04:52Z (0 bytes read), so the frontend's own error text for the /api/cart 500s is unknown.
The 1-minute frontend-proxy error series has missing samples between 04:46:45Z and 04:48:00Z, so the exact error timing around the alert start cannot be established.

The pre-04:48:07Z '500' log query returned nothing but its read was cut by the 4 MiB limit at 04:48:07.806Z, and the post-04:50:19.935Z part of the 500 burst is unknown (only the newest 100 of 426 matching lines were shown), so the burst's true duration and count are unknown.
The old cart pod's logs are unavailable (previous container 'cart' not found in cart-84889c965d-tkxdz), so its shutdown behaviour and any in-flight request failures are unknown.

The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no items (status no_data), so it cannot be stated whether network policy restrictions exist; the cart Service endpoint list is only the state at query time (~05:12Z), not during the incident.
No HTTP status-code or gRPC status-code metric series exist in this target's Prometheus, so the 500/503 distribution is only known from proxy access logs and span status tags.
Span-metric data for frontend-proxy starts only around 04:29-04:34Z, so the error behaviour before that (and whether the sporadic 503s predate the authorized window) is unknown.
next_steps: Read the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source for RequestErrorRate (outside the registered target if necessary) to obtain its expression, window and threshold, and evaluate it at 04:47:17Z against traces_span_metrics_calls_total.
Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream_connection_options idle_timeout and the frontend server keep-alive settings, and review whether upstream connection reuse is intended.
Confirm with the platform owner which change performed the cart Deployment rollout restart at 04:49:47Z and whether flagd-config cartFailure was toggled around then.
Decide whether the cart Deployment should get a readinessProbe and whether the demo's single-replica services need surge capacity for rollouts.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
